title.narrative: A multi-sectoral integrated intervention to prevent or reduce the impact of drought in most at-risk Bokh and Gashamo Woredas of Somali Regional State.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project delivers a multi-sectoral response to address the urgent needs of communities in Bokh and Gashamo Woredas, Somali Regional State, Ethiopia, facing the anticipated La Niña-induced drought. This drought, compounded by conflict, is expected to severely impact livelihoods, health, nutrition, and access to water, heightening the vulnerability of these communities. The project targets four key areas: Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), Health, Nutrition, and Agriculture, with integrated protection and gender equality considerations.ltbrgtIn the WASH component, the project will rehabilitate water points, install rainwater harvesting systems, and improve sanitation facilities to ensure sustainable access to clean water, particularly for women, children, and other vulnerable groups. Hygiene promotion campaigns will be implemented to prevent waterborne diseases, especially in overcrowded IDP and refugee areas affected by the anticipated drought.ltbrgtThe Health component includes deploying Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs) to provide primary healthcare services, with a focus on maternal and child health, immunization, and communicable disease treatment. Measles vaccination campaigns and Rapid Response Team (RRT) training will strengthen the capacity for outbreak preparedness, particularly in areas at high risk of disease spread due to drought conditions.ltbrgtThe Nutrition component will address Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) through Stabilization Centers and provide Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) to households, ensuring access to nutritious food during the drought. The Community-based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) approach will empower local health workers to monitor and treat malnutrition, reinforcing local capacity.ltbrgtIn the agricultural sector, the project will protect the resilience of livelihoods from anticipated drought shocks. Activities include destocking of sheep and goats to preserve household assets, providing nutrition-sensitive livestock feed, and distributing agricultural tools. Vaccination and treatment of livestock for prevalent diseases will be conducted. Additionally, improved drought-tolerant cash crop seeds will be distributed to agro-pastoral and pastoral communities to support food security and livelihoods during the drought.ltbrgtThe project emphasizes Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) by actively engaging communities in needs assessments, implementation, and monitoring. Community feedback mechanisms will be established to address concerns and ensure local ownership of the project.ltbrgtTo promote sustainability, the project will train local government staff and community health workers to manage services beyond the project’s duration, ensuring that infrastructure and services remain functional and resilient to future droughts.ltbrgtOWS Development Fund’s long-standing presence in Bokh and Gashamo, along with its strong partnerships with local authorities, will ensure effective project implementation. This project aligns with the Second Reserve Allocation Strategy 2024 by addressing the urgent needs of the drought-affected population while building long-term resilience.ltbrgtIn summary, the project aims to mitigate the impact of the La Niña-induced drought by addressing critical needs in WASH, health, nutrition, and agriculture, while promoting protection and gender equality to strengthen community resilience in the Somali Region. The project will reach a total of 47,522 at-risk population with a budget size of $448,044.30 for five months. ltbrgtlt/pgt
